chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Walid whose title is Shabab al-Sayrafi, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Jafri, that I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! What is the meaning of al-Samad?'
He (peace be upon him) answered: 'He is the Master on whom all depend in major and minor matters.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الصَّمَدُ: The Necessary, the Master upon whom all depend
key_terms.الْمَصْمُودُ إِلَيْهِ: The one upon whom dependence is placed

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of al-Samad in Surah Al-Ikhlas according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the attribute of *al-Samad* by defining it as the ultimate Master (*Sayyid*) to whom all creation turns for sustenance and authority in both trivial and significant matters. This interpretation aligns with the Shia exegetical tradition that emphasizes God’s self-sufficiency and His role as the sole source of reliance (*istighatha*) for the universe, distinguishing Him from created beings who are dependent. The term thus encapsulates both absolute independence and the universal dependency of all else upon Him.
